statements.text: Morning shift today, the 5:30 route to Ntinda was quiet except for that one guy who always argues about the fare. My phone battery died halfway through, need to get a new one soon.
Just got a Xiaomi Redmi Note 13, finally. The camera is decent, but the battery lasts all day even with the bus app running. My old Samsung was a brick.
My sister Grace just moved to Leeds for a nursing job. She says it rains all the time. I told her Kampala traffic is worse than any weather.
Started running in the mornings before my shift. Just a few kilometers around the neighborhood, but my legs are killing me. Trying to drop the belly.
Bought a secondhand Toyota Corolla for weekends. It's old but runs fine. Now I can visit my parents in Jinja without waiting for the taxi.
My dog Bubbles died yesterday. He was 14, a good boy. The house feels empty. I buried him under the mango tree in the backyard.
Got a new kitten from a neighbor. She's grey and white, named her Panya because she chases mice. Bubbles would have liked her.
Thinking about switching to Android from this Xiaomi. The camera is fine but the software is glitchy. Maybe a Samsung again.
Finally got the keys to the Kadıköy place. Wait, no, that's not me—my cousin in Istanbul. I'm still in Kampala. Just excited for him.
My first week on nights. The 11pm route to Bwaise is eerie but the roads are empty. I sleep during the day now, feels weird.
Quit running. Too tired after night shifts. Now I just do push-ups at home. Not the same but better than nothing.
My girlfriend Sarah moved in last week. She brought her cat, Mwizi. Now Panya and Mwizi hiss at each other all day. Chaos.
Switched to a Samsung Galaxy A54. The Xiaomi was driving me crazy with the notifications. This one feels solid.
Sarah and I broke up last night. She moved out this morning, took Mwizi. The flat is too quiet. Panya keeps looking for her.
Started a weekend gig driving for a private school bus. Extra cash for the rent. The kids are loud but it's only Saturday mornings.
Went to Jinja for the weekend. My mom made matoke and groundnut stew. The Corolla handled the road fine, no issues.
Got a new phone again—Pixel 7a. The Samsung was okay but the camera on this is amazing. I take photos of the sunrise on my night shifts.
My brother Joseph just started driving for the same bus company. He's on the Jinja route. We see each other at the depot sometimes.
Switched to a plant-based diet for Lent. No meat, no eggs. I'm surviving on beans and rice. Sarah would have laughed—she was vegetarian.
Back to eating meat. Lent is over. Had a huge beef stew yesterday. My stomach was not happy but my soul was.
The Corolla broke down on the way to Jinja. Timing belt. Cost me a month's savings to fix. Thinking of selling it and just using the bus again.
Sold the Corolla. Now I'm back to taking taxis on my days off. It's actually cheaper than maintaining that car.
Started a new hobby: learning Swahili on my phone. I use Duolingo during breaks. Ninajifunza Kiswahili. Pole pole.
My sister Grace is back from Leeds for a visit. She brought fish and chips. We ate them in the garden. Panya tried to steal a chip.
Switched back to day shifts. The night schedule was killing my social life. Now I can see my friends again. Also started running again, gently.
Panya had kittens. Four of them. Under the bed. I didn't even know she was pregnant. Now I have five cats. Help.
Gave two kittens to my neighbor. Two left. They're cute but they climb the curtains. Panya is a good mother.
Thinking about getting a motorcycle. A Bajaj Boxer. Cheaper than a car, good for Kampala traffic. But my mom will worry. We'll see.
